junction.name: Flatbush Avenue & Farragut Road, New York City

claims.text: Flatbush Avenue & Farragut Road had 37 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 13 pedestrians injured, 4 cyclists injured and 0 people killed.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $2.5 million a year.
No crash pattern here stands out against the city's priority junctions.

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: worked (pedestrian injury crashes changed -17% (95% interval -22% to -11%) at 1,651 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing).
The city's turn traffic calming: earlier trend (a simple before/after says -26%, but a placebo date before the work shows a drop too, so the decline cannot be credited to the program).
The city's enhanced crossings: not shown (at 96 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (-7%, 95% interval -50% to +69%) could be zero).
The city's speed humps: not shown (at 1,008 sites the change in injury crashes (+0%, 95% interval -9% to +9%) could be zero).
Leading Pedestrian Interval would avoid about 0.3 crashes a year (CMF 9918, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites), worth $116,000 a year.
Yellow Change Intervals would avoid about 2.0 crashes a year (CMF 4215, the median of 4 eligible records), worth $689,000 a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red.
The NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is responsible for Flatbush Avenue, Farragut Road (not listed in NYSDOT Roadway Inventory, so a city street).
Who can push for it: Council Member, District 45, New York City Council; Brooklyn Community Board 14.
A request letter to the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is ready to draft from these facts.
